# Independent code review iteration

Scope: independent full pass over the `octomation/go-service` template at `c582be5` (2024-12-07): hand-written Go code and tests, generated protocol wiring at integration boundaries, configuration, containers, Make/Task automation, CI, reusable delivery workflows, release config, and docs. Existing reviews were not used as input; overlap with prior reviews is intentional independent corroboration. Offline issue and roadmap dumps were excluded.

Validation: on Go 1.26.5, `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go test -race ./...` and `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go vet ./...` passed. Coverage is 27.7% in `internal/command` and 0% in `internal/server`/`internal/config`. A runtime probe, `go run ./cmd/client --config config.toml --host 127.0.0.1:65534 hello probe`, attempted `127.0.0.1:8890`, dynamically confirming finding 2. `GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.20.14 GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go test ./...` failed while parsing the `toolchain` directive, confirming finding 6.

Severity: **Crit** / **High** / **Med** / **Low** / **Nit**.
Class: `correctness` · `security` · `concurrency` · `perf` · `api` · `idiom` · `modern` · `test` · `build` · `docs`.

## 1. Listener failures leave a partially dead service reporting success

Twirp, gRPC, gateway, profiler, and Connect listeners are started in detached goroutines. Terminal errors from `ListenAndServe`/`Serve` are printed and discarded. If a port is occupied, an accept loop dies, or the Connect address is empty (which makes `ListenAndServe` fall back to `:http`), `server run` keeps waiting for a signal and returns no failure to its supervisor. The process can therefore appear healthy while one or more advertised protocols are unavailable.

Only the Connect `http.Server` is retained for shutdown; all other server values are unreachable once started.

**Fix.** Construct every server explicitly, run them in an `errgroup`, cancel the group when any listener returns a non-shutdown error, and report that error from `RunE`. On cancellation, shut down every HTTP server and gracefully stop gRPC with a bounded deadline.

## 2. Config loading silently discards command-line address overrides

Cobra writes `--host` directly into `cnf.Server.Connect.Address`, then `PersistentPreRunE` unmarshals the config file over the same struct. Config therefore wins over the command line. The runtime probe requested port 65534 but the client dialed the file's `127.0.0.1:8890`. The server command uses the same mutation order for its host flag.

**Fix.** Bind flags to Viper keys and perform one merge with the intended precedence (flags > environment > config > defaults), or load config before parsing overrides into the final struct. Add execution tests that assert the actual dial/listen address.

## 3. Production configuration publishes an unauthenticated pprof endpoint

`internal/command/server.go` imports `net/http/pprof`, mounts `http.DefaultServeMux`, and starts it whenever `server.profile.address` is set. `deploy/config.toml` binds it to `0.0.0.0:3360`; both Dockerfiles expose 3360 and Compose publishes it to the host. Anyone able to reach that port can inspect goroutines, heap/profile data, command arguments, and can trigger expensive CPU/trace profiles.

**Fix.** Disable pprof in the production template by default. Put diagnostics on a separately protected listener (loopback/admin network, authentication/mTLS, network policy), use a dedicated mux, and do not publish the port from the default container/Compose configuration.

## 4. Workflow event text is executable shell input

The local notify action interpolates commit messages, dispatch reasons, and workflow names directly into a Bash heredoc inside `run:`. GitHub expands `${{ ... }}` before Bash parses it, so shell syntax or a crafted heredoc delimiter in event data can change the program. Notification jobs receive the Slack webhook, and release/deploy jobs may have broader tokens.

**Fix.** Pass all event text through environment variables and write multiline outputs with a safe random delimiter; never splice message/name/title/ref fields into inline shell. Reference: [GitHub script-injection guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/script-injections).

## 5. Pull requests are allowed to deploy the production documentation site

Every CI run calls `cd.docs.yml` after tests with `pages: write` and `id-token: write`; the job condition is literally `if: true`. This includes `pull_request` runs. The reusable workflow checks out the PR commit, builds docs, and invokes `actions/deploy-pages` in the `github-pages` environment. A contributor branch that passes tests can overwrite the public site unless an external environment rule happens to block it.

**Fix.** Build/preview docs on pull requests without deployment permissions. Gate production deployment on `github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'`, require the lint and test jobs, and add an environment protection rule.

## 6. The test matrix contains a Go version that cannot parse this module

`go.mod` declares `go 1.21` and a `toolchain go1.23.3` directive, but CI explicitly runs Go 1.20. The toolchain directive and required language version are newer than that command, so the lane cannot load the module. A template quality gate that is red by construction teaches consumers to ignore CI.

**Fix.** Remove 1.20 or lower the module/toolchain only if the code is genuinely compatible. Define the support floor once and derive the matrix from it; test floor + current stable rather than contradictory versions.

## 7. Success and failure tests execute neither advertised command path

Both client and server tests assign `os.Args = []string{"version"}` and `[]string{"unknown"}`. `os.Args[0]` is the executable name, so Cobra receives no arguments in both cases. The root command has no Run function and simply returns nil. The callbacks that contain the exit-code assertions are never invoked, yet the subtests pass; reported 100% line coverage in `cmd/*` is therefore misleading.

**Fix.** Include a program name (`{"server", "version"}` / `{"server", "unknown"}`), record whether the exit callback ran, and assert output/error. Prefer a `run(ctx, args, stdout, stderr) int` function instead of mutable package globals, restoring any globals with `t.Cleanup` meanwhile.

## 8. Dependency-only updates bypass CI

The path filter uses literal `go.{mod,sum}` for pull requests and pushes. GitHub does not apply brace expansion, so `go.mod` and `go.sum` changes alone do not trigger the workflow. That leaves the exact changes most likely to alter compilation and vulnerability exposure untested.

**Fix.** List `go.mod` and `go.sum` separately, include `tools/*`, protocol generation inputs, Docker/release configs, and docs lockfiles in the relevant gates. Reference: [GitHub path pattern syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#patterns-to-match-file-paths).

## 9. Initialization leaves upstream distribution targets in generated services

The advertised `run init my.new/service` changes only the module path and Go imports. It leaves `octomation/go-service` and the generic `service` identity in GoReleaser, GHCR image tags, Docker/Compose files, Buf registry name, Homebrew formula, installer, config, badges, docs, and release links. A generated service can compile and test successfully but fail at release time—or target upstream resources if credentials permit.

**Fix.** Replace the ad-hoc sed with a transactional renderer that accepts module, owner/repository, binary/service name, image registry, and documentation host. Keep a manifest of templated fields and fail initialization if upstream identifiers remain. Test a generated repository through build, container, snapshot release, and docs publication.

## 10. Secured changes URLs but never enables transport security

`Protocol.Secured` only switches `BaseURL` from `http://` to `https://`. Every server still calls plaintext `http.ListenAndServe`, insecure gRPC credentials, or h2c; there is no certificate/key configuration. Setting `secured = true` therefore makes clients speak TLS to plaintext listeners rather than securing traffic.

**Fix.** Model TLS explicitly (certificate/key or injected `tls.Config`) and use `ListenAndServeTLS` / TLS gRPC credentials. If TLS termination is intentionally external, rename the field to describe the advertised scheme and document the trusted proxy boundary.

## 11. HTTP servers have no bounds and only one is shut down

All HTTP listeners use default zero timeouts and default header limits. Slow headers, writes, or idle connections can consume resources indefinitely. Shutdown reaches only Connect and uses the still-live command context without a deadline; Twirp, gateway, and profiler remain alive until process exit.

**Fix.** Build `http.Server` values with `ReadHeaderTimeout`, `ReadTimeout`, `WriteTimeout`, `IdleTimeout`, and `MaxHeaderBytes`; retain them in a lifecycle owner and shut all of them down under a short timeout.

## 12. CLI requests have no transport deadline

Both commands use `http.DefaultClient`, while main supplies `context.Background()` with no deadline. A stalled connection or server can keep the CLI alive indefinitely. Ctrl-C handling is also not wired through `signal.NotifyContext` in the client.

**Fix.** Inject an `http.Client` with transport/header timeouts, add a command timeout flag/default, and derive main context from termination signals.

## 13. Releases float on latest GoReleaser with an unversioned legacy config

The workflow uses `goreleaser-action@v5` with `version: latest`, while `.goreleaser.yml` has no `version: 2` header and uses legacy sections such as `brews`, per-archive `format`, and old Docker-manifest configuration. The exact release engine changes without a repository diff; current GoReleaser can warn or fail depending on which removed fields it encounters.

**Fix.** Migrate with a pinned GoReleaser v2, add `version: 2`, run `goreleaser check` and a snapshot in CI, then pin the action and engine to compatible immutable versions. Reference: [GoReleaser version errors](https://www.goreleaser.com/resources/errors/version/).

## 14. Development build metadata records unknown as the commit

When build info is available but ldflags did not set `commit`, init assigns `commit = "unknown, mod sum: <sum>"`. It also overwrites `version` with values such as `(devel)`. A diagnostic/version command then presents a synthetic string as a commit identifier, making provenance parsing unreliable.

**Fix.** Read VCS revision/time/dirty state from `debug.BuildInfo.Settings`, keep module sum in its own field, and preserve clear unknown values when metadata is absent.

## 15. Source installation uses go get for binaries

The README recommends `go get .../cmd/client@latest` and `go get .../cmd/server@latest`. Since Go 1.17, executable installation is `go install path@version`; `go get` edits dependencies of the current module and is not an installation command.

**Fix.** Replace both examples with `go install`, state the required Go version, and test the instructions in a clean temporary module during release validation.
